themes_detail.label: Street Light Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints surged to 38 THIS WEEK vs. a 12.4-week average, a 207% spike (z-score: 8.43), suggesting rapid deterioration of outdoor lighting infrastructure across Far Rockaway that could impact safety and quality of life.
evidence: 38 street light condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.4-week baseline average (207% increase, z-score 8.43)
High statistical severity threshold met; spike emerged sharply this week, not gradual
Correlates with damaged street sign spike (540% up last week), suggesting broader street infrastructure degradation event
reporting_angles: Interview residents about dark blocks and safety concerns; map complaint hotspots in Rockaway neighborhoods
Request DOT records on street light maintenance schedules and repair backlogs; investigate whether a single outage event or systemic failure triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints exploded to 4 reports TWO WEEKS AGO from a near-zero baseline (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72), marking the highest-severity statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting potential contamination or system failure.
evidence: 4 water quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% increase, z-score 11.72, highest severity in dataset)
Long-standing community board budget requests for DEP capital projects and sewer infrastructure upgrades signal pre-existing water system vulnerabilities
Converges with high complaint volume for Water System (323 total in 90 days, 9th-ranked category) and Plumbing (327 complaints)
reporting_angles: Obtain DEP water quality test results and boil-water notice records for Far Rockaway from 2 weeks ago; interview affected residents about discoloration, odor, or taste changes
Investigate what triggered the spike: main break, treatment plant issue, or contamination event; connect to community board's years of requests for sewer/water infrastructure funding

themes_detail.label: Noise Surge Across Multiple Types
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints THIS WEEK show mixed but elevated activity: street/sidewalk noise up 174% (37 vs. 13.5 average), commercial noise up 158% (10 vs. 3.9 average), while residential noise declined 20%, suggesting a shift toward outdoor/commercial disruption this week.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise: 37 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.5-week average (174% increase, z-score 5.1)
Commercial noise: 10 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.9-week average (158% increase, z-score 4.22)
Residential noise DOWN 20% THIS WEEK (77 vs. 95.8 average), suggesting complaints shifted from indoors to outdoors/commercial
reporting_angles: Identify commercial sources: bars, restaurants, construction, or events driving the spike; map complaints geographically to pinpoint hotspot blocks
Interview residents about what changed this week; check for new late-night permits, seasonal tourism uptick, or special events in the Rockaway peninsula

themes_detail.label: Street Signage Degradation Wave
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street sign complaints spiked 540% LAST WEEK (20 vs. 3.1 average, z-score: 10.99) and dangling signs up 206% (13 vs. 4.2 average), indicating rapid structural failure of street furniture that may affect navigation and safety.
evidence: Damaged street signs: 20 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.1-week average (540% increase, z-score 10.99)
Dangling street signs: 13 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.2-week average (206% increase, z-score 4.28)
Overlaps with street light spike THIS WEEK, suggesting broader infrastructure maintenance gap or weather event (wind, salt spray) affecting outdoor structures
reporting_angles: Request DOT maintenance records for street furniture in Far Rockaway; check for weather events or recent storms that may have triggered failures
Document which intersections have missing or damaged signs; assess whether hazardous conditions exist for drivers or pedestrians relying on navigation

themes_detail.label: Urban Tree Health Decline
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK from a 0.4-week average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42), a small but statistically significant anomaly reflecting potential environmental stress or disease outbreak affecting street canopy.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4-week baseline average (700% increase, z-score 5.42)
Converges with street light and sign infrastructure spikes THIS WEEK, possibly indicating weather stress event or maintenance cycle affecting multiple asset classes
Community board budget requests include park/amenity reconstruction and development (Edgemere Commons, Arverne East), suggesting ongoing focus on environmental infrastructure
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to determine if specific tree species or neighborhoods are affected; investigate whether disease, salt spray, or drought is the cause
Visual survey of street trees in complaint hotspots; connect to broader climate resilience and green space equity narrative in coastal Rockaway communities
